subject: Re: Dedicated pool backpressure — exec liaison & mitigation
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia@citrinelabs.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwoood-inference.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Realtime inference errors and latency - reserved capacity not meeting SLA

Hi Lukas —

We're seeing sustained 5xx spikes and p95 latency climbing to ~1.8s for our /v1/generate route since ~08:45 PT. Traffic pattern hasn't changed on our side (same QPS), and the dashboard shows our reserved throughput pegged while some requests queue for several seconds. This started right during morning batch of traffic and is currently impacting checkout flows.

Attached are our sampling of request ids and the SDK trace. Can you confirm whether this is a routing/backpressure issue on your dedicated pool or something in our integration? We need a plan and ETA — this is impacting our customers.

Thanks,
Alicia Gomez
Head of Platform
Citrine Labs

Attachment: citrine-request-sample-0902.csv
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.inference>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@citrinelabs.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 09:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool backpressure — exec liaison & mitigation

Alicia — thanks for the heads up and for the sample. I'm escalating to our SRE and sales leadership immediately. Short answer: we are seeing elevated queue depth for your reserved pool and a subset of requests returning 5xx retryable errors consistent with token queue timeouts.

Planned immediate actions:
- Dylan & infra team to triage and share a snapshot of GPU utilization, queue depth, and recent kernel fallback events.
- If we confirm reserved capacity starvation, request your permission to temporarily route traffic to our compatible burst pool (cross-account fallback) while we remediate. This will require a short config flip and may change cost profile for this window.
- We'll propose a follow-up exec bridge at 10:30 PT if the issue isn't closed by then.

Do you approve a temporary failover to the burst pool and for us to run a short KV cache clear on your model instances? If yes we'll start now and keep you updated with metrics every 10 minutes.

— Lukas
Lukas Meyer | Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
T: (415) 555-0109
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.inference>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Dedicated pool backpressure — exec liaison & mitigation

Team — preliminary triage (10:02 snapshot):
- Reserved pool assigned to Citrine Labs: 12 GPUs (A100 equivalent), sustained 98% GPU utilization across the farm for the last 20m.
- Queue depth: median queue depth 120 requests, 95th percentile queue time = 3.1s. Several requests hit the internal token-queue timeout and returned 5xx.
- Observed an increase in KV cache misses after 08:40 coincident with a large batched inference run from a single client shard (not Citrine-originated). Spillover and scheduling jitter caused our scheduler to deprioritize reserved tasks temporarily.
- No evidence of model degradation or kernel crash; kernel fallback to fp16 quant variant occurred for ~6% of requests which increased per-token latency slightly.

Immediate mitigations applied at 10:08:
1) Temporarily tightened scheduler fairness: reserved-tenant priority gating enforced to reduce cross-tenant spill. 2) Cleared stale per-tenant KV entries for Citrine (small risk of cold-start), 3) Opened an emergency burst allowance of +20% on top of reserved pool (ops authorization) but requires exec approval to maintain for >30m.

Short-term ask for exec (Logan/Marissa): authorize sustained burst allocation for up to 90 minutes while we shift noisy neighbors off the nodes and finish a rebalancing window. Without authorization the burst will revert automatically after 10 minutes and queueing will likely return. Estimated customer-visible improvement: reduce p95 latency to ~450-600ms and drop 5xx to background levels.

I've uploaded the telemetry bundle and a sampled trace set to the shared Drive. Attachments: pool-metrics-20270902.json, citrine-kv-backlog-20270902.csv.

— Dylan Brooks
SRE Lead, Inference Platform
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.inference>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.inference>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.inference>, Alicia Gomez <alicia@citrinelabs.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Dedicated pool backpressure — exec liaison & mitigation

Lukas / Dylan — thank you for the triage. Lukas, please go ahead and apply the temporary failover to the burst pool (customer approval received verbally at 10:12). We'll follow up on credits after this is stabilized; I want the immediate priority to be service restoration.

Logan — please confirm exec authorization for up to 90m burst. If we need longer we'll re-open with procurement for a short-term commitment increase.

Alicia — we will not change your model version; this action is strictly routing and short-lived. I'll hold off on any billing decisions until we have post-mortem. Expect a 10-minute cadence update.

— Marissa Cole
VP Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.inference>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@citrinelabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.inference>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool backpressure — exec liaison & mitigation

Alicia — quick update and next steps:
- We applied the temporary routing to the burst pool at 10:15; early metrics show p95 latency down to 520ms and 5xx rates dropping from 6.1% to 0.2% for successful requests.
- Dylan's team is rebalancing noisy tenants off the nodes now and will run a controlled rebalance over the next 45 minutes.
- Ops requested and received exec approval for a 60-minute sustained burst (authorized by Logan at 10:28). If we require longer we'll propose a short-term capacity boost + procurement approval.

Action items and ownership:
- Dylan: complete node rebalancing and post a follow-up telemetry set (ETA 11:45).
- Lukas: coordinate with Alicia on a customer-facing post-mortem and compensation proposal (cc Marissa).
- Marissa: prepare a credit proposal and hold a 1:1 with Citrine if they request escalation.

Alicia, apologies for the impact — we prioritized restoration and will deliver an RCA within 48 hours with mitigation/guardrails to prevent a repeat. Please reply if you'd like an exec bridge now or prefer the RCA first.

Thanks,
Lukas Meyer
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
